scenario: A second experiment proposes the exact same (domain, baseline, proposed) combination as an experiment that already exists in the project.
finding: With memory enabled, the platform correctly identifies exp2 as a duplicate of exp1 (same domain/baseline/proposed) BEFORE it would be executed, pointing the researcher/agent back to the existing result. With memory disabled, no such warning is possible - the duplicate would proceed to execution undetected.
caveat: n=1 project, one duplicate scenario. This demonstrates the mechanism works as designed; it is not a statistical claim about duplicate-experiment rates across many researchers/projects (that would require Section 35's full human-subjects-style ablation, not run here).
